# Material Binding Strength Override

## Triggers
material binding strength, binding not applying, material override, weakerThanDescendants, strongerThanDescendants, unassign material, clear material binding, material precedence, binding priority

## Context
USD material bindings have a strength property that determines which binding wins when multiple bindings exist on ancestor and descendant prims. The Assign Material LOP's `bindingstrength` parameter controls this. When a material "doesn't take," it is almost always a binding strength conflict with an existing assignment.

## Code

```python
import hou

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Setup: create a scene with geometry and two conflicting material bindings
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
stage = hou.node("/stage")

# Create geometry with a default material already assigned
geo = stage.createNode("sopimport", "hero_geo")
geo.parm("soppath").set("/obj/hero/OUT")

# First material library -- assigns a base material
matlib1 = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "base_materials")
matlib1.cook(force=True)  # CRITICAL: cook before creating shader children
mtlx = matlib1.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "base_shader")
matlib1.parm("assign1").set(1)
matlib1.parm("geopath1").set("/hero_geo/geo/shape")
matlib1.parm("matpath1").set("/materials/base_shader")

# Wire geo -> matlib1
matlib1.setInput(0, geo)

# Second material library -- overrides with a different material
matlib2 = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "override_materials")
matlib2.cook(force=True)
mtlx2 = matlib2.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "override_shader")
matlib2.parm("assign1").set(1)
matlib2.parm("geopath1").set("/hero_geo/geo/shape")
matlib2.parm("matpath1").set("/materials/override_shader")

# KEY: Set binding strength to override existing binding
# Options: "weakerThanDescendants" (default) | "strongerThanDescendants"
matlib2.parm("bindingstrength1").set("strongerThanDescendants")

matlib2.setInput(0, matlib1)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Assign Material LOP with explicit binding strength
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
assign = stage.createNode("assignmaterial", "assign_mtl")
assign.setInput(0, matlib2)

# Assign a material with strongerThanDescendants so it overrides any
# descendant-level binding already present
assign.parm("nummaterials").set(1)
assign.parm("primpattern1").set("/hero_geo/geo/shape")
assign.parm("matspecpath1").set("/materials/override_shader")
assign.parm("bindingstrength1").set("strongerThanDescendants")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read binding strength from USD stage to verify
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
assign.cook(force=True)
usd_stage = assign.stage()
prim = usd_stage.GetPrimAtPath("/hero_geo/geo/shape")

from pxr import UsdShade
binding_api = UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim)

# Direct binding (most common)
direct_binding = binding_api.GetDirectBinding()
print(f"Material: {direct_binding.GetMaterialPath()}")
# Expected: /materials/override_shader

# Check binding strength via USD API
rel = prim.GetRelationship("material:binding")
if rel:
    # Custom data stores binding strength
    print(f"Binding relationship: {rel.GetTargets()}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Unassign Material LOP -- clear all bindings on a prim
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
unassign = stage.createNode("unassignmaterial", "clear_bindings")
unassign.setInput(0, assign)
unassign.parm("nummaterials").set(1)
unassign.parm("primpattern1").set("/hero_geo/geo/shape")

# After unassign, the prim reverts to inherited or no material
unassign.cook(force=True)
usd_stage2 = unassign.stage()
prim2 = usd_stage2.GetPrimAtPath("/hero_geo/geo/shape")
binding2 = UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim2).GetDirectBinding()
print(f"After unassign: {binding2.GetMaterialPath()}")
# Expected: empty (no binding)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Collection-based binding with strength
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
assign_coll = stage.createNode("assignmaterial", "assign_collection")
assign_coll.setInput(0, geo)
assign_coll.parm("nummaterials").set(1)
assign_coll.parm("primpattern1").set("/hero_geo")
assign_coll.parm("matspecpath1").set("/materials/base_shader")
# Collection bindings on ancestors use weaker strength by default
# so descendant direct bindings win
assign_coll.parm("bindingstrength1").set("weakerThanDescendants")
```

## Expected Scene Graph

```
/hero_geo/
  geo/
    shape           <-- material:binding -> /materials/override_shader
                        (strongerThanDescendants wins over base_shader)
/materials/
  base_shader/      <-- UsdShade.Material
    base_shader/    <-- UsdShade.Shader (mtlxstandard_surface)
  override_shader/  <-- UsdShade.Material
    override_shader/<-- UsdShade.Shader (mtlxstandard_surface)
```

## Common Mistakes

- **Using default binding strength when overriding**: Default is `weakerThanDescendants`, which loses to any existing descendant binding. Use `strongerThanDescendants` to force override.
- **Assuming later node in chain always wins**: Binding strength takes priority over LOP evaluation order. A weak upstream binding can be preserved if downstream uses `weakerThanDescendants`.
- **Not checking for collection-based bindings**: Collection bindings on ancestor prims can conflict with direct bindings. Use `UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI.GetBoundMaterial()` to see the resolved material.
- **Forgetting Unassign Material LOP**: To truly clear a binding, use the Unassign Material LOP. Simply assigning a different material may leave the old binding on a different purpose (e.g., `preview` vs `full`).
- **Mixing binding purposes**: `allPurpose`, `preview`, and `full` bindings are separate. A `full` binding does not clear an existing `allPurpose` binding.

# Material Library LOP Setup

## Triggers
material library, matlib, create material, material library cook, cook force true, createNode shader, matlib subnet, geopath assignment, multiple materials, material library setup

## Context
The Material Library LOP is the standard way to create and assign materials in Solaris. The critical gotcha is that `matlib.cook(force=True)` MUST be called before `createNode()` on shader children -- without the cook, the internal subnet does not exist and `createNode()` returns None silently.

## Code

```python
import hou

stage = hou.node("/stage")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Basic material library with a single MaterialX material
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
matlib = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "materials")

# CRITICAL: cook the matlib BEFORE creating shader children.
# Without this, the internal subnet doesn't exist and createNode returns None.
matlib.cook(force=True)

# Now create a shader inside the matlib
shader = matlib.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "hero_mtl")
# shader is NOT None only because we cooked first
assert shader is not None, "matlib.cook(force=True) was not called!"

# Set shader parameters
shader.parm("base_color").set(hou.Vector3(0.8, 0.2, 0.1))
shader.parm("specular_roughness").set(0.3)
shader.parm("metalness").set(0.0)

# Assign to geometry via geopath (inside the matlib node itself)
matlib.parm("assign1").set(1)            # enable first assignment slot
matlib.parm("geopath1").set("/geo/hero/shape")  # exact USD prim path
matlib.parm("matpath1").set("/materials/hero_mtl")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Multiple materials in one matlib (preferred over separate matlib nodes)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
matlib_multi = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "multi_materials")
matlib_multi.cook(force=True)

# Material 1: metal
metal = matlib_multi.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "metal_mtl")
metal.parm("base_color").set(hou.Vector3(0.9, 0.85, 0.7))
metal.parm("metalness").set(1.0)
metal.parm("specular_roughness").set(0.15)

# Material 2: rubber
rubber = matlib_multi.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "rubber_mtl")
rubber.parm("base_color").set(hou.Vector3(0.05, 0.05, 0.05))
rubber.parm("metalness").set(0.0)
rubber.parm("specular_roughness").set(0.7)

# Material 3: glass
glass = matlib_multi.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "glass_mtl")
glass.parm("base_color").set(hou.Vector3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0))
glass.parm("transmission").set(0.95)
glass.parm("specular_roughness").set(0.0)
glass.parm("thin_walled").set(False)

# Assign all three via geopath slots
matlib_multi.parm("num_materials").set(3)
for i, (name, path) in enumerate([
    ("metal_mtl", "/geo/car/body"),
    ("rubber_mtl", "/geo/car/tires"),
    ("glass_mtl", "/geo/car/windows"),
], start=1):
    matlib_multi.parm(f"assign{i}").set(1)
    matlib_multi.parm(f"geopath{i}").set(path)
    matlib_multi.parm(f"matpath{i}").set(f"/materials/{name}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Correct wiring order in the LOP network
# geometry FIRST -> then matlib -> camera -> render_settings -> karma
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
sopimport = stage.createNode("sopimport", "import_geo")
sopimport.parm("soppath").set("/obj/hero/OUT")

sublayer = stage.createNode("sublayer", "env_usd")
sublayer.parm("filepath1").set("$HIP/usd/environment.usd")

merge = stage.createNode("merge", "merge_scene")
merge.setInput(0, sopimport)       # geometry first
merge.setInput(1, sublayer)        # additional geo

matlib.setInput(0, merge)          # matlib after geo

camera = stage.createNode("camera", "render_cam")
camera.setInput(0, matlib)         # camera after matlib

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Verify the material was created in USD
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
matlib.cook(force=True)
usd_stage = matlib.stage()
from pxr import UsdShade

mtl_prim = usd_stage.GetPrimAtPath("/materials/hero_mtl")
if mtl_prim:
    material = UsdShade.Material(mtl_prim)
    surface_output = material.GetSurfaceOutput()
    print(f"Material: {mtl_prim.GetPath()}")
    print(f"Surface output: {surface_output.GetAttr().GetConnections()}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Common pattern: matlib with textured material
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
matlib_tex = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "textured_materials")
matlib_tex.cook(force=True)

# Create standard surface
tex_shader = matlib_tex.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "wood_mtl")

# Create texture reader node and connect to base_color
tex_reader = matlib_tex.createNode("mtlximage", "wood_diffuse")
tex_reader.parm("file").set("$HIP/tex/wood_diffuse_4k.exr")

# Connect texture output to shader base_color input
tex_shader.setNamedInput("base_color", tex_reader, "out")

# Create normal map reader
normal_reader = matlib_tex.createNode("mtlxnormalmap", "wood_normal")
normal_img = matlib_tex.createNode("mtlximage", "wood_normal_tex")
normal_img.parm("file").set("$HIP/tex/wood_normal_4k.exr")
normal_reader.setNamedInput("in", normal_img, "out")
tex_shader.setNamedInput("normal", normal_reader, "out")

# Layout nodes inside matlib for readability
matlib_tex.layoutChildren()
```

## Expected Scene Graph

```
/geo/
  hero/
    shape           <-- material:binding -> /materials/hero_mtl
  car/
    body            <-- material:binding -> /materials/metal_mtl
    tires           <-- material:binding -> /materials/rubber_mtl
    windows         <-- material:binding -> /materials/glass_mtl
/materials/
  hero_mtl/         <-- UsdShade.Material
    hero_mtl/       <-- UsdShade.Shader (mtlxstandard_surface)
  metal_mtl/        <-- UsdShade.Material
    metal_mtl/      <-- UsdShade.Shader
  rubber_mtl/       <-- UsdShade.Material
    rubber_mtl/     <-- UsdShade.Shader
  glass_mtl/        <-- UsdShade.Material
    glass_mtl/      <-- UsdShade.Shader
  wood_mtl/         <-- UsdShade.Material
    wood_mtl/       <-- UsdShade.Shader
    wood_diffuse/   <-- UsdShade.Shader (mtlximage)
    wood_normal/    <-- UsdShade.Shader (mtlxnormalmap)
    wood_normal_tex/<-- UsdShade.Shader (mtlximage)
```

## Common Mistakes

- **Not calling `matlib.cook(force=True)` before `createNode()`**: This is the #1 material error. Without the cook, the matlib's internal subnet doesn't exist and `createNode()` returns `None` silently. Always cook first.
- **Using separate matlib + assign nodes instead of geopath slots**: The matlib has built-in assignment slots (`geopath1`, `matpath1`). Using separate Assign Material nodes is unnecessary for simple setups and adds network clutter.
- **Wrong wiring order**: Geometry must come before the matlib in the LOP chain. If matlib is upstream of the geo, the material targets don't exist yet and bindings fail silently.
- **Using wildcard geopath patterns**: `geopath` must be an exact USD prim path like `/geo/hero/shape`, not a glob like `/geo/hero/*`. Wildcards in geopath do not resolve.
- **Creating multiple matlib nodes for one scene**: Prefer one matlib with multiple shader subnets. Multiple matlibs create separate `/materials/` scopes that can conflict.

# Dynamic Material Assignment with VEXpressions

## Triggers
vexpression material, dynamic material assign, elemnum, ptnum lops, conditional material, multi material vex, attribute driven material, vexpression assign material

## Context
LOPs use VEXpressions for dynamic per-prim material assignment. The critical difference from SOPs is that LOPs iterate over USD prims using `@elemnum`, NOT `@ptnum`. Using `@ptnum` in a LOP VEXpression silently returns 0 for every prim, causing all prims to get the same material.

## Code

```python
import hou

stage = hou.node("/stage")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Setup: geometry with multiple prims that need different materials
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
sopimport = stage.createNode("sopimport", "multi_geo")
sopimport.parm("soppath").set("/obj/scene/OUT")

# Create materials
matlib = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "scene_materials")
matlib.cook(force=True)
matlib.setInput(0, sopimport)

red_mtl = matlib.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "red_mtl")
red_mtl.parm("base_color").set(hou.Vector3(0.8, 0.1, 0.1))

blue_mtl = matlib.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "blue_mtl")
blue_mtl.parm("base_color").set(hou.Vector3(0.1, 0.1, 0.8))

green_mtl = matlib.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "green_mtl")
green_mtl.parm("base_color").set(hou.Vector3(0.1, 0.8, 0.1))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# VEXpression: assign by @elemnum (prim index in LOP traversal)
# CRITICAL: LOPs use @elemnum, NOT @ptnum
# @ptnum is always 0 in LOPs -- this is the #1 VEXpression mistake
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
assign = stage.createNode("assignmaterial", "vex_assign")
assign.setInput(0, matlib)
assign.parm("nummaterials").set(1)
assign.parm("primpattern1").set("/geo/*")

# VEXpression that alternates materials by prim index
# @elemnum = prim iteration index (0, 1, 2, ...)
assign.parm("matspecpath1").setExpression('''
    // @elemnum iterates over matched prims in traversal order
    // @ptnum does NOT work in LOPs -- always returns 0
    string materials[] = array(
        "/materials/red_mtl",
        "/materials/blue_mtl",
        "/materials/green_mtl"
    );
    return materials[@elemnum % len(materials)];
''', hou.exprLanguage.Hscript)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# VEXpression: assign by prim name attribute
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
assign_name = stage.createNode("assignmaterial", "name_assign")
assign_name.setInput(0, matlib)
assign_name.parm("nummaterials").set(1)
assign_name.parm("primpattern1").set("/geo/**")

# Use prim name to determine material
assign_name.parm("matspecpath1").setExpression('''
    // s@name is available for each USD prim
    string name = s@name;
    if (match("*metal*", name))
        return "/materials/red_mtl";
    if (match("*glass*", name))
        return "/materials/blue_mtl";
    return "/materials/green_mtl";  // default fallback
''', hou.exprLanguage.Hscript)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# VEXpression: assign by USD prim path
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
assign_path = stage.createNode("assignmaterial", "path_assign")
assign_path.setInput(0, matlib)
assign_path.parm("nummaterials").set(1)
assign_path.parm("primpattern1").set("/**")

assign_path.parm("matspecpath1").setExpression('''
    // s@primpath gives the full USD prim path
    string path = s@primpath;
    if (match("*/body*", path))
        return "/materials/red_mtl";
    if (match("*/wheels*", path))
        return "/materials/blue_mtl";
    return "";  // empty string = no assignment (skip this prim)
''', hou.exprLanguage.Hscript)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# VEXpression: assign by custom primvar attribute
# Requires primvar to be set upstream (e.g., via Attribute Wrangle in SOPs)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
assign_attr = stage.createNode("assignmaterial", "attr_assign")
assign_attr.setInput(0, matlib)
assign_attr.parm("nummaterials").set(1)
assign_attr.parm("primpattern1").set("/geo/**")

# Read a custom integer primvar set on the geometry
assign_attr.parm("matspecpath1").setExpression('''
    // i@material_id is a primvar set at SOP level
    // propagated to LOPs via SOP Import
    int id = i@material_id;
    if (id == 0) return "/materials/red_mtl";
    if (id == 1) return "/materials/blue_mtl";
    if (id == 2) return "/materials/green_mtl";
    return "/materials/red_mtl";  // fallback
''', hou.exprLanguage.Hscript)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# SOP-level: set the material_id attribute for LOP consumption
# (run this in a SOP Attribute Wrangle before the SOP Import)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# In a SOP Attribute Wrangle (detail mode or point mode):
```

MaterialX shaders in Houdini become USD shader prims under the `mtlx:` namespace. Understanding how MaterialX nodes map to USD prims is essential for reading/writing material parameters through the USD API. A common gotcha is the `_shader` suffix on material prim paths -- the Material prim and its Shader child prim have different paths.

## Code

```python

stage = hou.node("/stage")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create a MaterialX material in a Material Library
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
matlib = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "materials")
matlib.cook(force=True)

shader = matlib.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "bronze")
shader.parm("base_color").set(hou.Vector3(0.7, 0.45, 0.2))
shader.parm("metalness").set(1.0)
shader.parm("specular_roughness").set(0.25)
shader.parm("coat").set(0.3)

# Cook to generate USD prims
matlib.cook(force=True)
usd_stage = matlib.stage()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Understand the USD prim hierarchy MaterialX generates
# Material prim (UsdShade.Material) != Shader prim (UsdShade.Shader)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
from pxr import UsdShade, Sdf, Usd

# The Material Library creates:
#   /materials/bronze          <-- UsdShade.Material (container)
#   /materials/bronze/bronze   <-- UsdShade.Shader (actual shader node)
# NOTE: the shader child has the SAME name as the material parent

material_path = Sdf.Path("/materials/bronze")
shader_path = Sdf.Path("/materials/bronze/bronze")

material_prim = usd_stage.GetPrimAtPath(material_path)
shader_prim = usd_stage.GetPrimAtPath(shader_path)

print(f"Material prim type: {material_prim.GetTypeName()}")  # "Material"
print(f"Shader prim type: {shader_prim.GetTypeName()}")      # "Shader"

# The Material has surface/displacement outputs
material = UsdShade.Material(material_prim)
surface = material.GetSurfaceOutput()
print(f"Surface output connected to: {surface.GetAttr().GetConnections()}")
# -> [/materials/bronze/bronze.outputs:out]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reading MaterialX parameters through USD API
# Parameters are inputs on the Shader prim with mtlx: prefix
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
shader_usd = UsdShade.Shader(shader_prim)

# Get the shader implementation ID (identifies the MaterialX node type)
impl_attr = shader_prim.GetAttribute("info:id")
print(f"Shader ID: {impl_attr.Get()}")
# -> "ND_standard_surface_surfaceshader"

if metalness_input:

roughness_input = shader_usd.GetInput("specular_roughness")
if roughness_input:

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Writing MaterialX parameters through USD API
# Use Sdf.ValueTypeNames for correct type matching
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Modify base_color via USD API
base_color_input.Set((0.6, 0.3, 0.1))  # Gf.Vec3f auto-converts from tuple

roughness_input.Set(0.4)

file_input.Set(Sdf.AssetPath("$HIP/tex/bronze_diffuse.exr"))

# Connect texture output to base_color input
tex_output = tex_shader.CreateOutput("out", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Color3f)
base_color_input.ConnectToSource(tex_output)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# The _shader suffix gotcha
# Some code paths return /materials/bronze_shader instead of
# /materials/bronze -- always strip the suffix when comparing paths
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
def normalize_material_path(path_str):
    """Strip _shader suffix that some code paths add."""
    if path_str.endswith("_shader"):
        return path_str[:-7]  # remove "_shader"
    return path_str

# When reading material bindings, the path may or may not have _shader
raw_path = "/materials/bronze_shader"
clean_path = normalize_material_path(raw_path)
print(f"Normalized: {clean_path}")  # -> /materials/bronze

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Enumerate all MaterialX inputs on a shader prim
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
for inp in shader_usd.GetInputs():
    name = inp.GetBaseName()
    value = inp.Get()
    type_name = inp.GetTypeName()
    connected = inp.GetConnectedSource()
    if value is not None or connected:
        conn_str = f" <- {connected[0].GetPrim().GetPath()}" if connected else ""
        print(f"  {name} ({type_name}) = {value}{conn_str}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sdf.ValueTypeNames reference for MaterialX types
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
TYPE_MAP = {
    "float":    Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Float,
    "color3f":  Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Color3f,
    "color4f":  Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Color4f,
    "normal3f": Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Normal3f,
    "vector3f": Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Vector3f,
    "point3f":  Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Point3f,
    "int":      Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Int,
    "bool":     Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Bool,
    "string":   Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String,
    "asset":    Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Asset,   # texture file paths
    "token":    Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Token,   # enum-like strings
    "matrix4d": Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Matrix4d,
}
```

```
  bronze/                     <-- UsdShade.Material (type: "Material")
    surface.outputs:surface   <-- connected to bronze/bronze.outputs:out
    bronze/                   <-- UsdShade.Shader (type: "Shader")
      info:id = "ND_standard_surface_surfaceshader"
      inputs:base_color       <-- color3f, connected to diffuse_tex.outputs:out
      inputs:metalness        <-- float = 1.0
```

## Context
The `shop_materialpath` attribute set at SOP level propagates through SOP Import to LOPs as a material binding. Primvar readers in MaterialX allow geometry attributes to drive shader parameters directly, enabling per-point or per-prim variation without multiple materials.

## Code

```python
import hou

# =====================================================================
# PART 1: shop_materialpath at SOP level -> propagates to LOPs
# =====================================================================

obj = hou.node("/obj")

# Create a SOP network with geometry
geo_node = obj.createNode("geo", "hero")
box = geo_node.createNode("box", "base_geo")

# Set shop_materialpath on the geometry via Attribute Wrangle
wrangle = geo_node.createNode("attribwrangle", "set_material")
wrangle.setInput(0, box)
wrangle.parm("snippet").set('''
// Set material path as a detail or prim attribute
// This becomes a USD material binding when imported to LOPs
s@shop_materialpath = "/materials/hero_mtl";
''')
wrangle.parm("class").set(1)  # 0=detail, 1=prim, 2=point, 3=vertex

# For multiple materials on different prims, use conditional assignment
wrangle_multi = geo_node.createNode("attribwrangle", "multi_material")
wrangle_multi.setInput(0, wrangle)
wrangle_multi.parm("snippet").set('''
// Assign different materials based on prim groups or attributes
// @primnum is available at SOP level (NOT @elemnum -- that is LOPs only)
if (@primnum < 3)
    s@shop_materialpath = "/materials/red_mtl";
else if (@primnum < 6)
    s@shop_materialpath = "/materials/blue_mtl";
else
    s@shop_materialpath = "/materials/green_mtl";
''')
wrangle_multi.parm("class").set(1)  # prim-level

out = geo_node.createNode("null", "OUT")
out.setInput(0, wrangle_multi)
out.setDisplayFlag(True)
out.setRenderFlag(True)

# =====================================================================
# PART 2: SOP Import picks up shop_materialpath automatically
# =====================================================================

stage = hou.node("/stage")

sopimport = stage.createNode("sopimport", "import_hero")
sopimport.parm("soppath").set("/obj/hero/OUT")

# shop_materialpath is automatically converted to material:binding
# on the corresponding USD prim during SOP Import

# =====================================================================
# PART 3: Custom primvar attributes for shader parameter driving
# =====================================================================

# Set per-point color variation at SOP level
color_wrangle = geo_node.createNode("attribwrangle", "set_primvars")
color_wrangle.setInput(0, out)
color_wrangle.parm("snippet").set('''
// These become USD primvars after SOP Import
// Accessible in MaterialX via primvar reader nodes
v@Cd = set(rand(@ptnum), rand(@ptnum+1), rand(@ptnum+2));
f@roughness_variation = fit01(rand(@ptnum+3), 0.1, 0.8);
f@metalness_mask = (@ptnum % 2 == 0) ? 1.0 : 0.0;
''')

out2 = geo_node.createNode("null", "OUT2")
out2.setInput(0, color_wrangle)

sopimport.parm("soppath").set("/obj/hero/OUT2")

# PART 4: MaterialX primvar reader in the shader
# =====================================================================

matlib.cook(force=True)
matlib.setInput(0, sopimport)

cd_reader = matlib.createNode("mtlxgeompropvalue", "read_Cd")

cd_reader.parm("geomprop").set("Cd")
# signature must match type: "color3" for v@Cd
cd_reader.parm("signature").set("color3")
# Connect primvar output to shader base_color
shader.setNamedInput("base_color", cd_reader, "out")

# Create primvar reader for roughness_variation
rough_reader = matlib.createNode("mtlxgeompropvalue", "read_roughness")
rough_reader.parm("geomprop").set("roughness_variation")
rough_reader.parm("signature").set("float")
shader.setNamedInput("specular_roughness", rough_reader, "out")

# Create primvar reader for metalness_mask
metal_reader = matlib.createNode("mtlxgeompropvalue", "read_metalness")
metal_reader.parm("geomprop").set("metalness_mask")
metal_reader.parm("signature").set("float")
shader.setNamedInput("metalness", metal_reader, "out")

# =====================================================================
# PART 5: Primvar with fallback default value
# =====================================================================

# If the primvar doesn't exist on certain prims, use a default
fallback_reader = matlib.createNode("mtlxgeompropvalue", "read_opacity")
fallback_reader.parm("geomprop").set("opacity_mask")
fallback_reader.parm("signature").set("float")
# Set default value in case primvar is missing
fallback_reader.parm("default").set(1.0)

# =====================================================================
# PART 6: Verify primvar propagation in USD
# =====================================================================
matlib.cook(force=True)
usd_stage = matlib.stage()

from pxr import UsdGeom

# Check if primvars made it to USD
for prim in usd_stage.Traverse():
    if prim.IsA(UsdGeom.Gprim):
        pvapi = UsdGeom.PrimvarsAPI(prim)
        for pv in pvapi.GetPrimvars():
            name = pv.GetPrimvarName()
            interp = pv.GetInterpolation()
            print(f"  {prim.GetPath()}: primvar '{name}' interp={interp}")

# =====================================================================
# PART 7: Edit Properties LOP for per-prim primvar override
# =====================================================================
edit_props = stage.createNode("editproperties", "override_primvars")
edit_props.setInput(0, matlib)
edit_props.parm("primpattern").set("/hero/geo/shape")
edit_props.parm("numprops").set(1)
edit_props.parm("propname1").set("primvars:roughness_variation")
edit_props.parm("proptype1").set("float")
edit_props.parm("propval_float1").set(0.5)  # override roughness for this prim

matlib.layoutChildren()
```

```
    shape                          <-- material:binding -> /materials/hero_mtl
      primvars:Cd                  <-- color3f[] (per-point vertex color)
      primvars:roughness_variation <-- float[] (per-point roughness)
      primvars:metalness_mask      <-- float[] (per-point metalness)

  hero_mtl/                        <-- UsdShade.Material
    hero_mtl/                      <-- UsdShade.Shader (mtlxstandard_surface)
      inputs:base_color            <-- connected to read_Cd.outputs:out
      inputs:specular_roughness    <-- connected to read_roughness.outputs:out
      inputs:metalness             <-- connected to read_metalness.outputs:out
    read_Cd/                       <-- UsdShade.Shader (mtlxgeompropvalue)

    read_roughness/                <-- UsdShade.Shader (mtlxgeompropvalue)
```

## Triggers
karma xpu, xpu material, xpu materialx, xpu vex shader, xpu unsupported, karma cpu vs xpu, xpu fallback, xpu aov, xpu sss, karma renderer compatibility

## Context
Karma XPU (GPU-accelerated) supports MaterialX shaders ONLY -- VEX-based shaders do not render on XPU. Several advanced features are CPU-only. When building materials for XPU, always verify compatibility first. If a feature is unsupported, Karma silently falls back to default shading or produces black output.

## Code

```python
import hou

stage = hou.node("/stage")

# =====================================================================
# Check current Karma renderer type
# =====================================================================
karma = hou.node("/stage/karmarendersettings")
if karma:
    renderer = karma.parm("renderer").eval()  # "cpu" or "xpu"
    print(f"Current Karma renderer: {renderer}")

# =====================================================================
# XPU-compatible material: MaterialX ONLY
# =====================================================================
matlib = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "xpu_materials")
matlib.cook(force=True)

# CORRECT: mtlxstandard_surface works on both CPU and XPU
mtlx_shader = matlib.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "xpu_safe_mtl")
mtlx_shader.parm("base_color").set(hou.Vector3(0.8, 0.3, 0.1))
mtlx_shader.parm("metalness").set(0.0)
mtlx_shader.parm("specular_roughness").set(0.35)

# CORRECT: mtlximage for textures (XPU compatible)
tex = matlib.createNode("mtlximage", "diffuse_tex")
tex.parm("file").set("$HIP/tex/diffuse.exr")
mtlx_shader.setNamedInput("base_color", tex, "out")

# WRONG: VEX-based shaders do NOT work on XPU
# These will render as default grey on XPU:
#   principledshader  (VEX)
#   classicshader     (VEX)
#   houdini_vex_*     (VEX)
# Only use these with Karma CPU

# =====================================================================
# XPU-supported MaterialX nodes (safe to use)
# =====================================================================
XPU_SAFE_NODES = [
    "mtlxstandard_surface",    # main PBR shader
    "mtlximage",               # texture reader
    "mtlxnormalmap",           # normal map processing
    "mtlxmix",                 # blend two shaders/values
    "mtlxmultiply",            # multiply values
    "mtlxadd",                 # add values
    "mtlxconstant",            # constant value
    "mtlxfractal3d",           # procedural noise
    "mtlxnoise2d",             # 2D noise
    "mtlxnoise3d",             # 3D noise
    "mtlxramp4",               # color ramp
    "mtlxdotproduct",          # dot product
    "mtlxpower",               # power function
    "mtlxclamp",               # clamp values
    "mtlxremap",               # remap range
    "mtlxluminance",           # RGB to luminance
    "mtlxhsvtorgb",            # color space conversion
    "mtlxrgbtohsv",            # color space conversion
    "mtlxgeompropvalue",       # primvar reader
    "mtlxtexcoord",            # UV coordinates
    "mtlxposition",            # world/object position
    "mtlxnormal",              # surface normal
    "mtlxdisp_float",          # displacement (float)
    "mtlxdisp_vector",         # displacement (vector)
]

# =====================================================================
# XPU limitations -- features that require CPU fallback
# =====================================================================
XPU_LIMITATIONS = {
    "custom_aovs": "XPU has limited custom AOV support. "
                   "Use built-in LPE passes instead.",
    "sss_randomwalk": "Random walk SSS mode is CPU-only. "
                      "XPU supports basic SSS only.",
    "nested_dielectrics": "Nested dielectric priority is CPU-only. "
                          "XPU uses simple transmission.",
    "volume_shading": "Complex volume shaders are CPU-only. "
                      "XPU supports basic density volumes.",
    "custom_bsdf": "Custom BSDF via mtlxsurface is limited on XPU.",
    "opensubdiv_limit": "XPU subdivision limit differs from CPU. "
                        "Test at target subdiv level.",
}

# =====================================================================
# Helper: validate material for XPU compatibility
# =====================================================================
def check_xpu_compatibility(matlib_node):
    """Check all shaders in a matlib for XPU compatibility issues."""
    issues = []
    matlib_node.cook(force=True)

    for child in matlib_node.children():
        node_type = child.type().name()

        # Check for VEX shaders (incompatible with XPU)
        if node_type in ("principledshader::2.0", "principledshader",
                         "classicshader", "surfacemodel"):
            issues.append(
                f"  FAIL: {child.path()} uses VEX shader '{node_type}' "
                f"-- not supported on XPU. Use mtlxstandard_surface."
            )

        # Check for known XPU-limited features
        if node_type == "mtlxstandard_surface":
            sss = child.parm("subsurface")
            if sss and sss.eval() > 0:
                sss_method = child.parm("subsurface_method")
                if sss_method and sss_method.eval() == "randomwalk":
                    issues.append(
                        f"  WARN: {child.path()} uses randomwalk SSS "
                        f"-- CPU-only. XPU will use basic SSS."
                    )

        # Recursively check children (for nested shader networks)
        for sub in child.allSubChildren():
            sub_type = sub.type().name()
            if "vex" in sub_type.lower() or "houdini" in sub_type.lower():
                issues.append(
                    f"  FAIL: {sub.path()} uses '{sub_type}' "
                    f"-- not supported on XPU."
                )

    return issues

# Run the check
issues = check_xpu_compatibility(matlib)
if issues:
    print("XPU compatibility issues found:")
    for issue in issues:
        print(issue)
else:
    print("All materials are XPU-compatible.")

# =====================================================================
# Set up Karma render settings for XPU
# =====================================================================
render_settings = stage.createNode("karmarendersettings", "karma_xpu_settings")
render_settings.setInput(0, matlib)

# Set renderer to XPU
render_settings.parm("renderer").set("xpu")

# XPU-specific settings
render_settings.parm("xpu:devicetype").set("GPU")  # GPU or CPU+GPU
render_settings.parm("pathtracedsamples").set(64)

# For debugging: force CPU to compare output
# render_settings.parm("renderer").set("cpu")

# =====================================================================
# Fallback pattern: dual render settings for CPU/XPU switching
# =====================================================================
rs_cpu = stage.createNode("karmarendersettings", "karma_cpu")
rs_cpu.parm("renderer").set("cpu")
rs_cpu.parm("pathtracedsamples").set(256)

rs_xpu = stage.createNode("karmarendersettings", "karma_xpu")
rs_xpu.parm("renderer").set("xpu")
rs_xpu.parm("pathtracedsamples").set(64)

# Use a switch to toggle between CPU and XPU render settings
switch = stage.createNode("switchlop", "cpu_xpu_switch")
switch.setInput(0, rs_cpu)
switch.setInput(1, rs_xpu)
switch.parm("input").set(1)  # 0=CPU, 1=XPU

# =====================================================================
# UDIM texture support on XPU
# =====================================================================
# XPU supports UDIM textures with the standard <UDIM> token
udim_tex = matlib.createNode("mtlximage", "udim_diffuse")
udim_tex.parm("file").set("$HIP/tex/hero_diffuse.<UDIM>.exr")
# UDIM works on both CPU and XPU as of Houdini 20.5+
```

## Expected Scene Graph

```
/materials/
  xpu_safe_mtl/           <-- UsdShade.Material
    xpu_safe_mtl/         <-- UsdShade.Shader (ND_standard_surface_surfaceshader)
      inputs:base_color   <-- connected to diffuse_tex
    diffuse_tex/          <-- UsdShade.Shader (ND_image_color3)
/Render/
  rendersettings/         <-- UsdRender.Settings
    karma:renderer = "xpu"
    karma:pathtracedsamples = 64
```

## Common Mistakes

- **Using VEX shaders with XPU**: `principledshader`, `classicshader`, and any VEX-based shader renders as default grey on XPU. Always use `mtlxstandard_surface` or other MaterialX nodes.
- **Assuming CPU and XPU produce identical output**: There are subtle differences in SSS, volumes, and custom AOVs. Always render a comparison frame when switching renderers.
- **Not checking XPU device availability**: If no compatible GPU is found, XPU silently falls back to CPU. Check `karma:xpu:devicetype` and GPU driver version.
- **Using randomwalk SSS on XPU**: Random walk subsurface scattering is CPU-only. XPU uses a simpler SSS approximation that may look different.
- **Custom AOV expectations on XPU**: XPU has limited custom AOV support. Use built-in LPE-based render passes for reliable output. Test AOV output on XPU before committing to a pipeline.

# USD Path Expressions vs Houdini Prim Patterns

## Triggers
prim pattern, path expression, material assignment path, wildcard prim, exact prim path, collection targeting, material binding path, usd glob, prim path material, houdini glob pattern

## Context
Material bindings in USD require exact prim paths, not wildcard patterns. Houdini LOPs use "prim patterns" which support wildcards, but the resulting material binding is always written to a specific prim. Confusing prim patterns (for selecting which prims to bind) with the actual binding target path is the most common material assignment failure.

## Code

```python
import hou

stage = hou.node("/stage")

# =====================================================================
# Setup: scene with nested geometry hierarchy
# =====================================================================
sopimport = stage.createNode("sopimport", "car")
sopimport.parm("soppath").set("/obj/car/OUT")
# Produces:
#   /car/geo/body
#   /car/geo/wheels/front_left
#   /car/geo/wheels/front_right
#   /car/geo/wheels/rear_left
#   /car/geo/wheels/rear_right
#   /car/geo/windows/windshield
#   /car/geo/windows/side_left
#   /car/geo/windows/side_right

# =====================================================================
# CORRECT: Exact prim paths for material binding targets
# =====================================================================
matlib = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "car_materials")
matlib.cook(force=True)
matlib.setInput(0, sopimport)

paint = matlib.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "car_paint")
paint.parm("base_color").set(hou.Vector3(0.8, 0.1, 0.1))
paint.parm("metalness").set(0.3)
paint.parm("coat").set(1.0)

rubber = matlib.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "tire_rubber")
rubber.parm("base_color").set(hou.Vector3(0.02, 0.02, 0.02))
rubber.parm("specular_roughness").set(0.8)

glass = matlib.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "window_glass")
glass.parm("transmission").set(0.95)

# CORRECT: exact path for body
matlib.parm("assign1").set(1)
matlib.parm("geopath1").set("/car/geo/body")
matlib.parm("matpath1").set("/materials/car_paint")

# =====================================================================
# Assign Material LOP with prim patterns (wildcards for SELECTION)
# =====================================================================
assign_wheels = stage.createNode("assignmaterial", "assign_wheels")
assign_wheels.setInput(0, matlib)

assign_wheels.parm("nummaterials").set(1)
# Prim pattern with wildcard -- selects WHICH prims get the binding
# This is NOT the binding target path -- it's the selection filter
assign_wheels.parm("primpattern1").set("/car/geo/wheels/*")
assign_wheels.parm("matspecpath1").set("/materials/tire_rubber")

# The result: each matched prim gets its own individual binding:
#   /car/geo/wheels/front_left  -> material:binding -> /materials/tire_rubber
#   /car/geo/wheels/front_right -> material:binding -> /materials/tire_rubber
#   etc.

# =====================================================================
# WRONG: common mistakes with path patterns
# =====================================================================

# WRONG: This does NOT work for material binding geopath
# matlib.parm("geopath1").set("/car/*")
# geopath does NOT support wildcards -- must be exact path

# WRONG: Houdini glob-style that doesn't exist in USD
# assign.parm("primpattern1").set("/car/geo/{body,wheels}")
# USD prim patterns don't support brace expansion

# =====================================================================
# Prim pattern syntax reference (for Assign Material / Edit Properties)
# =====================================================================
PRIM_PATTERNS = {
    # Exact path (most reliable)
    "/car/geo/body":          "Single exact prim",

    # Wildcard -- one level deep
    "/car/geo/*":             "All direct children of /car/geo",

    # Recursive wildcard -- all descendants
    "/car/geo/**":            "All descendants of /car/geo at any depth",

    # Pattern matching
    "/car/geo/wheels/*left":  "Prims ending in 'left' under wheels",
    "/car/geo/wheels/front_*":"Prims starting with 'front_' under wheels",

    # Multiple patterns (space-separated)
    "/car/geo/body /car/geo/wheels/*": "body + all wheel children",

    # Exclusion (prefix with ^)
    "/car/geo/** ^/car/geo/windows/*": "All car geo except windows",

    # By USD prim type
    "%type:Mesh":             "All Mesh-type prims in entire stage",
    "%type:Xform":            "All Xform-type prims",
}

# =====================================================================
# Demo: using each pattern type with Assign Material
# =====================================================================
assign_all = stage.createNode("assignmaterial", "assign_demo")
assign_all.setInput(0, assign_wheels)

# Pattern 1: all windows via wildcard
assign_all.parm("nummaterials").set(3)

assign_all.parm("primpattern1").set("/car/geo/windows/*")
assign_all.parm("matspecpath1").set("/materials/window_glass")

# Pattern 2: exclusion pattern -- everything except windows and wheels
assign_all.parm("primpattern2").set("/car/geo/** ^/car/geo/windows/* ^/car/geo/wheels/*")
assign_all.parm("matspecpath2").set("/materials/car_paint")

# Pattern 3: type-based selection
assign_all.parm("primpattern3").set("%type:Mesh")
assign_all.parm("matspecpath3").set("/materials/car_paint")

# =====================================================================
# Collection-based material assignment
# =====================================================================
collection = stage.createNode("collection", "hero_collection")
collection.setInput(0, sopimport)

# Define a collection on an ancestor prim
collection.parm("primpath1").set("/car")
collection.parm("collectionname1").set("paintable_parts")
# Include pattern for the collection
collection.parm("includepattern1").set("/car/geo/body /car/geo/wheels/*")
# Exclude pattern
collection.parm("excludepattern1").set("")

# Use collection in material assignment
assign_coll = stage.createNode("assignmaterial", "assign_via_collection")
assign_coll.setInput(0, collection)
assign_coll.parm("nummaterials").set(1)
# Reference the collection in the prim pattern
assign_coll.parm("primpattern1").set("%collection:/car.collection:paintable_parts")
assign_coll.parm("matspecpath1").set("/materials/car_paint")

# =====================================================================
# Verify: inspect all material bindings on the stage
# =====================================================================
assign_all.cook(force=True)
usd_stage = assign_all.stage()

from pxr import UsdShade

print("Material bindings:")
for prim in usd_stage.Traverse():
    binding = UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim).GetDirectBinding()
    mat_path = binding.GetMaterialPath()
    if mat_path:
        print(f"  {prim.GetPath()} -> {mat_path}")

# =====================================================================
# CRITICAL: material binding paths must be EXACT, not wildcards
# The binding relationship stores an exact path to the material prim
# =====================================================================
from pxr import Sdf
prim = usd_stage.GetPrimAtPath("/car/geo/body")
rel = prim.GetRelationship("material:binding")
targets = rel.GetTargets() if rel else []
# targets = [Sdf.Path("/materials/car_paint")]  -- always exact
print(f"Binding targets (always exact): {targets}")
```

## Expected Scene Graph

```
/car/
  geo/
    body                      <-- material:binding -> /materials/car_paint
    wheels/
      front_left              <-- material:binding -> /materials/tire_rubber
      front_right             <-- material:binding -> /materials/tire_rubber
      rear_left               <-- material:binding -> /materials/tire_rubber
      rear_right              <-- material:binding -> /materials/tire_rubber
    windows/
      windshield              <-- material:binding -> /materials/window_glass
      side_left               <-- material:binding -> /materials/window_glass
      side_right              <-- material:binding -> /materials/window_glass
/materials/
  car_paint/
  tire_rubber/
  window_glass/
```

## Common Mistakes

- **Using wildcards in matlib geopath**: The `geopath` parameter in Material Library does NOT support wildcards. It must be an exact prim path like `/car/geo/body`. Use Assign Material LOP for wildcard-based assignment.
- **Using `/rubbertoy/*` instead of `/rubbertoy/geo/shape`**: The most common error. Material bindings need to target the actual Mesh/Gprim, not its parent Xform. Check the exact prim hierarchy with scene inspection.
- **Confusing Houdini glob with USD prim patterns**: Houdini uses `*` and `**` similar to filesystem globs, but brace expansion `{a,b}` is not supported. Use space-separated paths for multiple targets.
- **Binding on Xform instead of Mesh**: Material bindings on Xform prims may not render. Always target the leaf Mesh or BasisCurves prim for reliable rendering.
- **Assuming `/**` includes the root prim**: `/car/**` matches all descendants of `/car` but NOT `/car` itself. To include the root, use `/car /car/**`.
- **Collection reference syntax**: Collection-based patterns use `%collection:/prim.collection:name` syntax, not `@collection` or `#collection`.

# Multi-Renderer Material Switching with Collect VOP

## Triggers
collect vop, multi renderer material, karma cpu xpu material, render delegate switch, material output collect, multiple surface outputs, cross renderer material, material purpose

## Context
The Collect VOP pattern allows a single Material prim to provide multiple shader implementations for different render delegates. This is essential when a pipeline must support Karma CPU (VEX or MaterialX), Karma XPU (MaterialX only), and third-party renderers (Arnold, RenderMan) from the same material network.

## Code

```python
import hou

stage = hou.node("/stage")

# =====================================================================
# Single-renderer material (simple case -- most common)
# =====================================================================
matlib = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "materials")
matlib.cook(force=True)

# Simple MaterialX material (works on both Karma CPU and XPU)
simple_mtl = matlib.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "universal_mtl")
simple_mtl.parm("base_color").set(hou.Vector3(0.8, 0.2, 0.1))
simple_mtl.parm("specular_roughness").set(0.3)
# This single shader works for both CPU and XPU Karma

# =====================================================================
# Multi-renderer material using Collect VOP
# Build one material that provides outputs for multiple renderers
# =====================================================================
matlib_multi = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "multi_renderer_materials")
matlib_multi.cook(force=True)

# The subnet inside the matlib is where we build the multi-output network
multi_mtl = matlib_multi.createNode("subnet", "hero_material")

# Enter the subnet to build the shader network
# Branch 1: MaterialX path (for Karma XPU and CPU)
mtlx_surface = multi_mtl.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "mtlx_shader")
mtlx_surface.parm("base_color").set(hou.Vector3(0.8, 0.2, 0.1))
mtlx_surface.parm("metalness").set(0.5)
mtlx_surface.parm("specular_roughness").set(0.25)

# MaterialX displacement
mtlx_disp = multi_mtl.createNode("mtlxdisp_float", "mtlx_displacement")
disp_tex = multi_mtl.createNode("mtlximage", "disp_texture")
disp_tex.parm("file").set("$HIP/tex/hero_displacement.exr")
mtlx_disp.setNamedInput("displacement", disp_tex, "out")

# Branch 2: VEX path (for Karma CPU only, richer feature set)
vex_surface = multi_mtl.createNode("principledshader::2.0", "vex_shader")
vex_surface.parm("basecolor").set(hou.Vector3(0.8, 0.2, 0.1))
vex_surface.parm("rough").set(0.25)
vex_surface.parm("metallic").set(0.5)

# Collect VOP: gathers multiple surface outputs into one material
collect = multi_mtl.createNode("collect", "collect_outputs")

# Connect both shader outputs to the collect node
# The collect node merges them into a single material with multiple outputs
collect.setInput(0, mtlx_surface)     # MaterialX surface
collect.setInput(1, mtlx_disp)        # MaterialX displacement
collect.setInput(2, vex_surface)      # VEX surface (Karma CPU fallback)

# The output of the subnet feeds back to the matlib
# Karma automatically picks the appropriate shader based on renderer type:
#   - XPU -> picks MaterialX outputs (ignores VEX)
#   - CPU -> can use either; prefers VEX if both exist (configurable)

multi_mtl.layoutChildren()

# =====================================================================
# Material Purpose: alternative to Collect VOP
# Use 'purpose' to explicitly tag which output is for which context
# =====================================================================

# In USD, material outputs can have purposes:
#   - "surface" (default)
#   - "displacement"
#   - "volume"
# And render contexts:
#   - "karma:surface"    (Karma-specific surface)
#   - "ri:surface"       (RenderMan-specific)
#   - "arnold:surface"   (Arnold-specific)

# =====================================================================
# Programmatic setup via USD API (for advanced control)
# =====================================================================
matlib_multi.cook(force=True)
usd_stage = matlib_multi.stage()

from pxr import UsdShade, Sdf

# Read the material and check its outputs
mat_path = "/materials/hero_material"
mat_prim = usd_stage.GetPrimAtPath(mat_path)
if mat_prim:
    material = UsdShade.Material(mat_prim)

    # List all outputs on the material
    for output in material.GetOutputs():
        print(f"  Output: {output.GetBaseName()} "
              f"type={output.GetTypeName()}")
        connections = output.GetAttr().GetConnections()
        if connections:
            print(f"    -> {connections}")

    # Get surface output for specific render context
    # Default context (universal):
    default_surface = material.GetSurfaceOutput()
    print(f"Default surface: {default_surface.GetAttr().GetConnections()}")

    # Karma-specific context:
    karma_surface = material.GetSurfaceOutput("karma")
    if karma_surface:
        print(f"Karma surface: {karma_surface.GetAttr().GetConnections()}")

# =====================================================================
# Assign multi-output material to geometry
# Assignment is the same regardless of single vs multi-output
# =====================================================================
assign = stage.createNode("assignmaterial", "assign_hero")
assign.setInput(0, matlib_multi)
assign.parm("nummaterials").set(1)
assign.parm("primpattern1").set("/hero/geo/shape")
assign.parm("matspecpath1").set("/materials/hero_material")

# =====================================================================
# Verify which shader Karma will use
# =====================================================================
def check_material_outputs(stage, material_path):
    """List all shader outputs a material provides."""
    mat_prim = stage.GetPrimAtPath(material_path)
    if not mat_prim:
        print(f"Material not found: {material_path}")
        return

    material = UsdShade.Material(mat_prim)
    results = {}

    # Check standard outputs
    for purpose in ["surface", "displacement", "volume"]:
        output = material.GetOutput(f"{purpose}")
        if output and output.GetAttr().GetConnections():
            results[purpose] = str(output.GetAttr().GetConnections()[0])

    # Check render-context-specific outputs
    for ctx in ["karma", "ri", "arnold"]:
        for purpose in ["surface", "displacement"]:
            output = material.GetOutput(f"{ctx}:{purpose}")
            if output and output.GetAttr().GetConnections():
                results[f"{ctx}:{purpose}"] = str(
                    output.GetAttr().GetConnections()[0]
                )

    print(f"Material outputs for {material_path}:")
    for key, val in sorted(results.items()):
        print(f"  {key} -> {val}")
    return results

check_material_outputs(usd_stage, "/materials/hero_material")
```

## Expected Scene Graph

```
/materials/
  hero_material/                <-- UsdShade.Material
    outputs:surface             <-- connected to mtlx_shader (default)
    outputs:displacement        <-- connected to mtlx_displacement
    outputs:karma:surface       <-- connected to vex_shader (CPU override)
    mtlx_shader/                <-- UsdShade.Shader (ND_standard_surface)
    mtlx_displacement/          <-- UsdShade.Shader (ND_displacement_float)
    disp_texture/               <-- UsdShade.Shader (ND_image_float)
    vex_shader/                 <-- UsdShade.Shader (principledshader)
    collect_outputs/            <-- Collects multiple outputs
  universal_mtl/                <-- UsdShade.Material (single renderer)
    universal_mtl/              <-- UsdShade.Shader (ND_standard_surface)
/hero/
  geo/
    shape                       <-- material:binding -> /materials/hero_material
```

## Common Mistakes

- **Not using Collect VOP when mixing VEX + MaterialX**: Without Collect, only one surface output is exposed. The render delegate may pick the wrong one or get nothing.
- **Assuming VEX shaders work on XPU**: XPU ignores VEX outputs entirely. The Collect VOP pattern ensures XPU gets the MaterialX path while CPU can use the richer VEX path.
- **Forgetting displacement in multi-output materials**: Surface and displacement are separate outputs. If you only connect the surface to the Collect, displacement is lost.
- **Render context naming**: Context names are renderer-specific (`karma:`, `ri:`, `arnold:`). Using the wrong prefix means the renderer ignores the output.
- **Over-engineering single-renderer pipelines**: If your pipeline only uses Karma (CPU or XPU), a simple `mtlxstandard_surface` works for both. The Collect VOP is only needed when supporting multiple render delegates or VEX+MaterialX simultaneously.

# Texture Parameter Overrides in Karma

## Triggers
texture override, edit properties lop, per prim parameter override, instanced material override, texture path override, udim texture, texture streaming, cpu xpu texture difference, material instance override

## Context
Overriding texture paths on instanced materials allows per-asset variation without duplicating entire material networks. The Edit Properties LOP is the primary tool for per-prim parameter overrides in Solaris. CPU and XPU Karma handle textures differently, particularly for UDIMs and texture streaming.

## Code

```python
import hou

stage = hou.node("/stage")

# =====================================================================
# Setup: base material with a texture
# =====================================================================
sopimport = stage.createNode("sopimport", "assets")
sopimport.parm("soppath").set("/obj/scene/OUT")

matlib = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "base_materials")
matlib.cook(force=True)
matlib.setInput(0, sopimport)

# Base shader with diffuse texture
shader = matlib.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "wood_mtl")
diffuse_tex = matlib.createNode("mtlximage", "wood_diffuse")
diffuse_tex.parm("file").set("$HIP/tex/wood_oak_diffuse.exr")
shader.setNamedInput("base_color", diffuse_tex, "out")

rough_tex = matlib.createNode("mtlximage", "wood_roughness")
rough_tex.parm("file").set("$HIP/tex/wood_oak_roughness.exr")
rough_tex.parm("signature").set("float")  # single channel
shader.setNamedInput("specular_roughness", rough_tex, "out")

# Assign base material to all furniture
matlib.parm("assign1").set(1)
matlib.parm("geopath1").set("/scene/furniture/table/shape")
matlib.parm("matpath1").set("/materials/wood_mtl")

matlib.parm("assign2").set(1)
matlib.parm("geopath2").set("/scene/furniture/chair/shape")
matlib.parm("matpath2").set("/materials/wood_mtl")

# =====================================================================
# Override texture path per-prim using Edit Properties LOP
# Same material, different texture on each piece of furniture
# =====================================================================
edit_table = stage.createNode("editproperties", "table_texture")
edit_table.setInput(0, matlib)

# Target the specific prim that has the material binding
edit_table.parm("primpattern").set("/scene/furniture/table/shape")
edit_table.parm("numprops").set(1)

# Override the texture file path on the material's shader input
# Path format: material_path.shader_name.input_name
edit_table.parm("propname1").set(
    "inputs:file"
)
# NOTE: Edit Properties targets the BOUND material's shader inputs
# You specify which prim's material to override, not the material prim directly
edit_table.parm("proptype1").set("asset")
edit_table.parm("propval_asset1").set("$HIP/tex/wood_walnut_diffuse.exr")
```

# Consolidated Material Error Patterns

## Triggers
material error, grey shader, default material, material not rendering, material binding failed, matlib cook error, wrong prim path, ptnum elemnum, material scope mismatch, material troubleshooting, material debug

## Context
This is a consolidated reference for the most common material errors in Houdini Solaris. Each error pattern includes the symptom, root cause, and fix with runnable code. Use this as a first-pass diagnostic when materials are not rendering correctly.

## Code

```python
import hou

stage = hou.node("/stage")

# =====================================================================
# ERROR 1: Grey/default shader appearing (binding didn't take)
# Symptom: geometry renders with Karma's default grey material
# =====================================================================

# CAUSE A: Material path in binding doesn't match actual material prim
# The binding says /materials/hero_mtl but the prim is /materials/hero_mtl_1

def diagnose_grey_shader(lop_node, geo_prim_path):
    """Check why a prim has no material or default material."""
    lop_node.cook(force=True)
    usd_stage = lop_node.stage()
    from pxr import UsdShade

    prim = usd_stage.GetPrimAtPath(geo_prim_path)
    if not prim:
        print(f"ERROR: Prim doesn't exist: {geo_prim_path}")
        print("  FIX: Check the exact prim hierarchy with stage inspection")
        return

    binding_api = UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim)

    # Check direct binding
    direct = binding_api.GetDirectBinding()
    mat_path = direct.GetMaterialPath()
    if not mat_path:
        print(f"NO BINDING on {geo_prim_path}")
        print("  FIX: Add material assignment (matlib geopath or Assign Material LOP)")
        return

    # Check if the material prim actually exists
    mat_prim = usd_stage.GetPrimAtPath(mat_path)
    if not mat_prim:
        print(f"DANGLING BINDING: {geo_prim_path} -> {mat_path}")
        print(f"  Material prim {mat_path} does NOT exist on stage")
        print("  FIX: Check material library output. Common causes:")
        print("    - matlib.cook(force=True) not called before createNode")
        print("    - Material path has _shader suffix mismatch")
        print("    - Material library is not wired into the LOP chain")
        return

    # Check if material has a valid surface output
    material = UsdShade.Material(mat_prim)
    surface = material.GetSurfaceOutput()
    if not surface or not surface.GetAttr().GetConnections():
        print(f"EMPTY MATERIAL: {mat_path} has no surface output")
        print("  FIX: Ensure shader node is connected inside the material subnet")
        return

    print(f"BINDING OK: {geo_prim_path} -> {mat_path}")
    print("  If still grey, check:")
    print("    - Renderer compatibility (VEX on XPU = grey)")
    print("    - Binding strength (weaker binding overridden by ancestor)")
    print("    - Material scope mismatch (/materials/ vs /mtl/)")

# Usage:
# diagnose_grey_shader(hou.node("/stage/karma"), "/geo/hero/shape")

# =====================================================================
# ERROR 2: matlib cook error -- createNode returns None
# Symptom: shader variable is None, crash on .parm() call
# =====================================================================

# WRONG: createNode before cook
matlib_wrong = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "wrong_matlib")
shader_none = matlib_wrong.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "test")
# shader_none is None! The internal subnet doesn't exist yet.
# Calling shader_none.parm("base_color") will raise AttributeError

# CORRECT: always cook first
matlib_right = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "right_matlib")
matlib_right.cook(force=True)  # <-- THIS LINE IS MANDATORY
shader_ok = matlib_right.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "test")
assert shader_ok is not None, "cook(force=True) was not called!"

# Safe wrapper function
def create_shader_in_matlib(matlib_node, shader_type, shader_name):
    """Safely create a shader inside a material library."""
    matlib_node.cook(force=True)
    shader = matlib_node.createNode(shader_type, shader_name)
    if shader is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Failed to create {shader_type} in {matlib_node.path()}. "
            f"This usually means cook(force=True) was not called or "
            f"the shader type '{shader_type}' is invalid."
        )
    return shader

# =====================================================================
# ERROR 3: @ptnum vs @elemnum in LOPs
# Symptom: all prims get the same material in VEXpression
# =====================================================================

# WRONG: @ptnum in LOPs (always returns 0)
# assign.parm("matspecpath1").setExpression('''
#     if (@ptnum == 0) return "/materials/red";   // ALL prims hit this
#     return "/materials/blue";                     // never reached
# ''')

# CORRECT: @elemnum in LOPs (actual prim iteration index)
# assign.parm("matspecpath1").setExpression('''
#     if (@elemnum == 0) return "/materials/red";   // first prim only
#     return "/materials/blue";                       // all other prims
# ''')

# Quick test to verify VEXpression is working
def test_vexpression_assignment(assign_node):
    """Cook and verify that different prims got different materials."""
    assign_node.cook(force=True)
    usd_stage = assign_node.stage()
    from pxr import UsdShade

    bindings = {}
    for prim in usd_stage.Traverse():
        binding = UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim).GetDirectBinding()
        mat = str(binding.GetMaterialPath())
        if mat:
            bindings[str(prim.GetPath())] = mat

    # Check if all prims got the same material (likely @ptnum bug)
    unique_materials = set(bindings.values())
    if len(unique_materials) == 1 and len(bindings) > 1:
        print("WARNING: All prims have the same material!")
        print("  This usually means @ptnum was used instead of @elemnum")
    else:
        print(f"OK: {len(unique_materials)} unique materials "
              f"across {len(bindings)} prims")

    for path, mat in sorted(bindings.items()):
        print(f"  {path} -> {mat}")

# =====================================================================
# ERROR 4: Wrong prim path in material assignment
# Symptom: binding created but on wrong prim (no visible effect)
# =====================================================================

def find_bindable_prims(lop_node, root_path="/"):
    """List all prims that can receive material bindings (Mesh, etc.)."""
    lop_node.cook(force=True)
    usd_stage = lop_node.stage()
    from pxr import UsdGeom

    bindable = []
    for prim in usd_stage.Traverse():
        if prim.IsA(UsdGeom.Gprim):  # Mesh, BasisCurves, Points, etc.
            bindable.append(str(prim.GetPath()))

    print(f"Bindable prims under {root_path}:")
    for p in bindable:
        if p.startswith(root_path):
            print(f"  {p}")
    return bindable

# Common path mistakes:
# WRONG: /rubbertoy          (Xform, not renderable)
# WRONG: /rubbertoy/*        (wildcard in geopath, not supported)
# WRONG: /rubbertoy/geo      (Xform, not the Mesh)
# RIGHT: /rubbertoy/geo/shape (actual Mesh prim)

# =====================================================================
# ERROR 5: Material scope mismatch (/materials/ vs /mtl/)
# Symptom: material exists but binding path doesn't match
# =====================================================================

def audit_material_scope(lop_node):
    """Check for material scope mismatches."""
    lop_node.cook(force=True)
    usd_stage = lop_node.stage()
    from pxr import UsdShade

    # Find all material prims
    material_paths = []
    for prim in usd_stage.Traverse():
        if prim.IsA(UsdShade.Material):
            material_paths.append(str(prim.GetPath()))

    # Find all material bindings
    binding_targets = []
    for prim in usd_stage.Traverse():
        binding = UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim).GetDirectBinding()
        target = str(binding.GetMaterialPath())
        if target:
            binding_targets.append(target)

    # Check for mismatches
    print("Material prims on stage:")
    for p in sorted(material_paths):
        print(f"  {p}")

    print("\nBinding targets referenced:")
    for t in sorted(set(binding_targets)):
        exists = t in material_paths
        status = "OK" if exists else "MISSING"
        print(f"  {t} [{status}]")

    # Common mismatch: /materials/ vs /mtl/
    scopes = set()
    for p in material_paths:
        parts = p.split("/")
        if len(parts) >= 2:
            scopes.add("/" + parts[1])
    if len(scopes) > 1:
        print(f"\nWARNING: Multiple material scopes found: {scopes}")
        print("  Standardize on /materials/ (Houdini default)")

# =====================================================================
# ERROR 6: Material not visible in Karma viewport
# Symptom: material works in render but viewport shows grey
# =====================================================================

# Check 1: viewport uses "preview" purpose, render uses "full"
# Some materials only define "full" purpose outputs
# FIX: ensure material has both outputs, or Karma viewport settings
#      are set to use "full" purpose

# Check 2: viewport material limit
# Karma viewport has a maximum material complexity budget
# Very complex shader networks may be simplified in viewport

# Check 3: display flag
# Ensure the matlib node (or downstream) has the display flag set
# If display flag is on a node BEFORE the matlib, materials won't show

# =====================================================================
# ERROR 7: Binding strength conflict (silent override)
# Symptom: material assignment appears correct but wrong material renders
# =====================================================================

def diagnose_binding_conflicts(lop_node, prim_path):
    """Check for binding strength conflicts on a prim."""
    lop_node.cook(force=True)
    usd_stage = lop_node.stage()
    from pxr import UsdShade, Sdf

    prim = usd_stage.GetPrimAtPath(prim_path)
    if not prim:
        print(f"Prim not found: {prim_path}")
        return

    binding_api = UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim)

    # Check direct binding
    direct = binding_api.GetDirectBinding()
    print(f"Direct binding: {direct.GetMaterialPath()}")

    # Check for collection-based bindings on ancestors
    current = prim
    while current:
        parent_binding = UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(current)
        # Check all collection bindings
        coll_bindings = parent_binding.GetCollectionBindings()
        for cb in coll_bindings:
            print(f"  Collection binding on {current.GetPath()}: "
                  f"{cb.GetMaterialPath()} "
                  f"(collection: {cb.GetCollectionPath()})")
        current = current.GetParent()
        if str(current.GetPath()) == "/":
            break

    # Compute the final resolved material
    resolved, _ = binding_api.ComputeBoundMaterial()
    if resolved:
        print(f"RESOLVED material: {resolved.GetPath()}")
    else:
        print("RESOLVED material: NONE")

# =====================================================================
# MASTER DIAGNOSTIC: run all checks on a scene
# =====================================================================

def full_material_diagnostic(lop_node):
    """Run complete material diagnostics on a LOP node."""
    print("=" * 60)
    print("MATERIAL DIAGNOSTIC REPORT")
    print("=" * 60)

    lop_node.cook(force=True)
    usd_stage = lop_node.stage()
    from pxr import UsdShade, UsdGeom

    issues = []

    for prim in usd_stage.Traverse():
        if not prim.IsA(UsdGeom.Gprim):
            continue

        path = str(prim.GetPath())
        binding_api = UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim)
        direct = binding_api.GetDirectBinding()
        mat_path = direct.GetMaterialPath()

        if not mat_path:
            issues.append(f"NO_BINDING: {path}")
            continue

        mat_prim = usd_stage.GetPrimAtPath(mat_path)
        if not mat_prim:
            issues.append(f"DANGLING: {path} -> {mat_path} (not on stage)")
            continue

        material = UsdShade.Material(mat_prim)
        surface = material.GetSurfaceOutput()
        if not surface or not surface.GetAttr().GetConnections():
            issues.append(f"EMPTY_MTL: {path} -> {mat_path} (no surface)")
            continue

    if issues:
        print(f"\n{len(issues)} issue(s) found:")
        for issue in issues:
            print(f"  {issue}")
    else:
        print("\nAll material bindings OK.")

    print("=" * 60)

# Usage:
# full_material_diagnostic(hou.node("/stage/karma"))
```

## Expected Scene Graph

```
# Healthy scene (no errors):
/geo/
  hero/
    shape       <-- material:binding -> /materials/hero_mtl   [OK]
  env/
    ground      <-- material:binding -> /materials/ground_mtl [OK]
/materials/
  hero_mtl/     <-- UsdShade.Material (has surface output)
  ground_mtl/   <-- UsdShade.Material (has surface output)

# Broken scene (common errors):
/geo/
  hero/
    shape       <-- material:binding -> /mtl/hero_mtl    [DANGLING - scope mismatch]
  env/
    ground      <-- (no binding)                          [NO_BINDING]
/materials/
  hero_mtl/     <-- UsdShade.Material (exists at /materials/, not /mtl/)
```

## Common Mistakes

- **Grey shader = no binding or dangling binding**: Run `diagnose_grey_shader()` first. 90% of grey shader issues are path mismatches.
- **matlib.cook(force=True) not called**: The #1 Python scripting error. Without it, `createNode()` returns None and downstream code crashes with `AttributeError: 'NoneType'`.
- **@ptnum in LOPs**: Always 0. Use `@elemnum`. This causes all prims to get the same material in VEXpression-based assignment.
- **Binding on Xform instead of Mesh**: `/rubbertoy` is an Xform. The Mesh is at `/rubbertoy/geo/shape`. Use `find_bindable_prims()` to discover correct paths.
- **/materials/ vs /mtl/ scope**: USD files from different DCCs may use different scope names. Houdini defaults to `/materials/`. Maya/Blender may use `/mtl/` or `/Looks/`. Check with `audit_material_scope()`.
- **Binding strength silently overriding**: An ancestor prim with `strongerThanDescendants` binding beats any descendant binding. Use `diagnose_binding_conflicts()` to trace the resolution chain.
- **Viewport vs render material mismatch**: Viewport uses `preview` purpose; final render uses `full`. Ensure materials define outputs for both, or configure viewport to use `full` purpose.

## Triggers
material binding strength, binding not applying, material override, weakerThanDescendants, strongerThanDescendants, unassign material, clear material binding, material precedence, binding priority

## Context
USD material bindings have a strength property that determines which binding wins when multiple bindings exist on ancestor and descendant prims. The Assign Material LOP's `bindingstrength` parameter controls this. When a material "doesn't take," it is almost always a binding strength conflict with an existing assignment.

## Code

```python
import hou

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Setup: create a scene with geometry and two conflicting material bindings
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
stage = hou.node("/stage")

# Create geometry with a default material already assigned
geo = stage.createNode("sopimport", "hero_geo")
geo.parm("soppath").set("/obj/hero/OUT")

# First material library -- assigns a base material
matlib1 = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "base_materials")
matlib1.cook(force=True)  # CRITICAL: cook before creating shader children
mtlx = matlib1.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "base_shader")
matlib1.parm("assign1").set(1)
matlib1.parm("geopath1").set("/hero_geo/geo/shape")
matlib1.parm("matpath1").set("/materials/base_shader")

# Wire geo -> matlib1
matlib1.setInput(0, geo)

# Second material library -- overrides with a different material
matlib2 = stage.createNode("materiallibrary", "override_materials")
matlib2.cook(force=True)
mtlx2 = matlib2.createNode("mtlxstandard_surface", "override_shader")
matlib2.parm("assign1").set(1)
matlib2.parm("geopath1").set("/hero_geo/geo/shape")
matlib2.parm("matpath1").set("/materials/override_shader")

# KEY: Set binding strength to override existing binding
# Options: "weakerThanDescendants" (default) | "strongerThanDescendants"
matlib2.parm("bindingstrength1").set("strongerThanDescendants")

matlib2.setInput(0, matlib1)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Assign Material LOP with explicit binding strength
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
assign = stage.createNode("assignmaterial", "assign_mtl")
assign.setInput(0, matlib2)

# Assign a material with strongerThanDescendants so it overrides any
# descendant-level binding already present
assign.parm("nummaterials").set(1)
assign.parm("primpattern1").set("/hero_geo/geo/shape")
assign.parm("matspecpath1").set("/materials/override_shader")
assign.parm("bindingstrength1").set("strongerThanDescendants")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read binding strength from USD stage to verify
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
assign.cook(force=True)
usd_stage = assign.stage()
prim = usd_stage.GetPrimAtPath("/hero_geo/geo/shape")

from pxr import UsdShade
binding_api = UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim)

# Direct binding (most common)
direct_binding = binding_api.GetDirectBinding()
print(f"Material: {direct_binding.GetMaterialPath()}")
# Expected: /materials/override_shader

# Check binding strength via USD API
rel = prim.GetRelationship("material:binding")
if rel:
    # Custom data stores binding strength
    print(f"Binding relationship: {rel.GetTargets()}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Unassign Material LOP -- clear all bindings on a prim
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
unassign = stage.createNode("unassignmaterial", "clear_bindings")
unassign.setInput(0, assign)
unassign.parm("nummaterials").set(1)
unassign.parm("primpattern1").set("/hero_geo/geo/shape")

# After unassign, the prim reverts to inherited or no material
unassign.cook(force=True)
usd_stage2 = unassign.stage()
prim2 = usd_stage2.GetPrimAtPath("/hero_geo/geo/shape")
binding2 = UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim2).GetDirectBinding()
print(f"After unassign: {binding2.GetMaterialPath()}")
# Expected: empty (no binding)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Collection-based binding with strength
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
assign_coll = stage.createNode("assignmaterial", "assign_collection")

assign_coll.parm("nummaterials").set(1)
```
